payload.title: Agent twins carry Markus source, not plain Markdown
payload.description:
Ryan (2026-10-21): the agent-readable twins should be Markus (Anthus-flavoured Markdown), not Markus stripped down to plain Markdown. Raised by the Papyrus marketing redesign session.

Current behaviour (develop, src/papyrus_content/projection/standard/):
1. markdown.py body_of() rewrites every ::image{...} directive to plain ![alt](src), dropping layout, caption and sizes. Every other Markus directive passes through verbatim.
2. blocks.py twin() drops ::band and ::column, flattens ::button into Markdown links, and omits ::island entirely, so interactive sections give agents nothing.
3. The naming says 'Markdown' throughout: docs, page actions ('Copy Markdown', 'View as Markdown'), llms.txt and the text/markdown content type.

Wanted:
- The twin keeps Markus directives verbatim: images with all attributes, and page blocks as written.
- Islands get a text fallback that agents can read, e.g. a directive body or a summary/fallback attribute, carried into the twin and rendered for no-JS readers.
- Decide the naming. Proposed: keep the .md extension and text/markdown content type for compatibility (Markus is a Markdown superset), but have docs, page-action labels and llms.txt say Markus where it adds meaning, e.g. 'Copy Markus' or 'View source (Markus)'. Ryan to confirm.
- Related gap: page blocks are a Papyrus pre-pass, not Markus, so the CMS save path (Markus validation) rejects them and they only work for directory-of-files sites. Either move page blocks into Markus proper or let the CMS validator accept them.

Coordinate with the Data Parade session (basePath work in projection/standard) and the Shipped work (hook-rendered item twins 404). Ends with a p.apyr.us docs update.
